source.anchor: Lee--Shen--Tian Lemma 2 proof; SPHMC arXiv:2609.06906v1 Lemma 4.17; ASTIS supporting expansion
source.original_text: ASTIS supporting expansion for Lee--Shen--Tian Lemma 2, used by SPHMC Lemma 4.17: when two normalized restricted-Gaussian fibers are written as exponential tilts of a common base, their relative entropy is the integral under the left fiber of the explicit normalized log-density ratio, provided that representative is integrable. This is the value-level KL-to-explicit-ratio step before the source differentiates its smooth ratio; it does not itself assert ratio integrability, a score identity, LSI, Fisher, T2, or W2 contraction.

lean.statement: Let X be a measurable space and mu a nonzero sigma-finite measure on X. Let f and g be real-valued functions on X. Assume f is measurable, exp(f) and exp(g) are integrable with respect to mu, and the function r(x) = f(x) - log(integral exp(f) dmu) - g(x) + log(integral exp(g) dmu) is integrable with respect to the normalized exponential tilt mu.tilted f. Then the extended-nonnegative-real Kullback-Leibler divergence klDiv(mu.tilted f, mu.tilted g) is not infinity, and its real value equals the integral of r with respect to mu.tilted f.

blind_reconstruction.text: Let X be a measurable space, let mu be a nonzero sigma-finite measure on X, and let f,g : X -> R. Assume that f is measurable, x |-> exp(f(x)) and x |-> exp(g(x)) are mu-integrable, and r : X -> R defined by r(x) = f(x) - log(integral_X exp(f) dmu) - g(x) + log(integral_X exp(g) dmu) is integrable with respect to mu.tilted f. Then klDiv(mu.tilted f, mu.tilted g) != infinity, and toReal(klDiv(mu.tilted f, mu.tilted g)) = integral_X r d(mu.tilted f).

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.TiltedLogRatio
import Mathlib.InformationTheory.KullbackLeibler.Basic

/-!
# KL divergence between two exponential tilts

This file converts Mathlib's canonical Radon--Nikodym log-likelihood ratio into
the explicit normalized log-density-ratio representative used in smooth paper
calculations.  The conversion is measure-theoretic only: it does not transport
classical derivatives across almost-everywhere equality.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.TiltedKL

open MeasureTheory

noncomputable section

variable {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X]

/-- If the explicit normalized log-ratio of two integrable exponential tilts
is integrable under the left tilt, then their canonical KL divergence is
finite and its real value is the integral of that explicit representative.

The integrability premise is deliberately stated for the displayed
representative.  Almost-everywhere equality is used only to transfer
integrability and the integral, never to transfer classical derivatives. -/
theorem finite_klDiv_and_toReal_eq_integral_normalizedLogRatio
    (mu : Measure X) [SigmaFinite mu] [NeZero mu] (f g : X → ℝ)
    (hf : Measurable f)
    (hfi : Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (f x)) mu)
    (hgi : Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (g x)) mu)
    (hrep : Integrable
      (fun x =>
        f x - Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (f z) ∂mu) - g x +
          Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (g z) ∂mu))
      (mu.tilted f)) :
    InformationTheory.klDiv (mu.tilted f) (mu.tilted g) ≠ ⊤ ∧
      (InformationTheory.klDiv (mu.tilted f) (mu.tilted g)).toReal =
        ∫ x,
          (f x - Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (f z) ∂mu) - g x +
            Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (g z) ∂mu)) ∂(mu.tilted f) := by
  let _ : IsProbabilityMeasure (mu.tilted f) := isProbabilityMeasure_tilted hfi
  let _ : IsProbabilityMeasure (mu.tilted g) := isProbabilityMeasure_tilted hgi
  have hae := TiltedLogRatio.llr_tilted_tilted_ae mu f g hf hfi hgi
  have hac : mu.tilted f ≪ mu.tilted g :=
    (tilted_absolutelyContinuous mu f).trans (absolutelyContinuous_tilted hgi)
  have hllr : Integrable (MeasureTheory.llr (mu.tilted f) (mu.tilted g))
      (mu.tilted f) :=
    hrep.congr hae.symm
  constructor
  · exact InformationTheory.klDiv_ne_top hac hllr
  · rw [InformationTheory.toReal_klDiv_of_measure_eq hac (by simp)]
    exact integral_congr_ae hae

end

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.TiltedKL

candidate_publication_context.statement: For two normalized exponential tilts of one nonzero sigma-finite base, integrability of the explicit normalized log ratio under the left tilt makes the canonical KL finite and identifies its real value with the integral of that explicit representative. This isolates the measure-theoretic step used before differentiating the restricted-fiber score.
assumptions: The common base is nonzero and sigma-finite.
Both exponential weights are integrable, and the left exponent is measurable.
The displayed normalized log ratio is integrable under the left tilted probability law.

obligations.label: Convert the canonical finite KL to the explicit normalized log-ratio integral without transporting gradients

lesson.title: Evaluate canonical KL with an explicit normalized tilt ratio
lesson.statement: Let mu be a nonzero sigma-finite measure and let f and g define integrable exponential tilts. If their displayed normalized log-density ratio is integrable under the left tilt, then the canonical KL divergence from the left tilt to the right tilt is finite, and its real value is exactly the left-tilt integral of that displayed ratio.
assumptions: The common base measure is sigma-finite and nonzero.
The left exponent f is measurable, and exp(f) and exp(g) are integrable under the base measure, so both normalized tilts are probability measures.
The explicit normalized ratio f-log Z_f-g+log Z_g is integrable under the left tilt. This real analytic obligation is not inferred merely from normalization.
No differentiability or gradient statement is used.

steps.title: Normalize the two tilts and obtain absolute continuity
steps.text: Integrability of both exponential weights makes each tilt a probability measure. The left tilt is absolutely continuous with respect to the common base, and the base is absolutely continuous with respect to the right tilt; composing gives the KL direction.
steps.lean: Use isProbabilityMeasure_tilted, tilted_absolutelyContinuous, absolutelyContinuous_tilted and trans.

steps.title: Transfer integrability only at the value level
steps.text: The previously compiled representative theorem identifies Mathlib's canonical llr with the explicit normalized ratio almost everywhere under the left tilt. Therefore the assumed integrability of the explicit ratio implies integrability of the canonical llr.
steps.lean: Apply Integrable.congr to TiltedLogRatio.llr_tilted_tilted_ae in the reverse direction.

steps.title: Certify finite canonical KL
steps.text: Mathlib's finite-KL criterion requires precisely absolute continuity in the KL direction and integrability of its canonical llr. Both have now been proved.

steps.title: Replace the canonical llr integral by the smooth representative
steps.text: Because both tilted measures have mass one, Mathlib's equal-mass KL formula has no extra mass correction. Almost-everywhere equality then changes the integrand without changing the integral.

lesson.lean_statement: The conclusion contains both the ENNReal finiteness certificate and the exact real integral identity. Its explicit integrability premise prevents toReal from silently collapsing infinity to zero.
lesson.lean_proof: Build probability instances for both tilts, compose absolute continuity, transfer L1 integrability through the existing a.e. representative theorem, then apply Mathlib's KL theorems and integral congruence.
